name: textarea
title: Textarea
description: Multi-line text input with auto, sm, md and lg sizes, with optional autosize (native field-sizing: content with a measured script fallback where unsupported) and vertical resize. Renders through Base UI Field.Control, so it works inside Field. `minRows` and `maxRows` optionally bound autosize by content lines plus padding and border; maxRows scrolls overflow. Without minRows the minimum stays 88px, and without maxRows growth is unbounded. Positive finite bounds only; minRows is clamped to maxRows when greater. Bounds are ignored without autosize, and rows remains ignored with autosize. The fallback measures on mount, typing and controlled value replacement; native support sets no inline height. See TextareaAutosizeBounded for bounded prompts and controlled updates. Opt-in `clearable` reserves space for a reset button and returns focus to the textarea. `onClear` runs after the value change; `clearLabel` overrides the localized name. Optional variant: outline (default), filled (secondary surface), or ghost (transparent chrome). FieldVariantProvider supplies the default; explicit props win. Ghost is for obvious editing contexts such as an edit-mode row or toolbar. Alternate variants retain focus, invalid and forced-colors boundaries. Size auto (default) uses density field padding: 12px comfortable and 10px compact, with 13px text and 24px line height. Textarea height follows its rows; it is not a single-line control. Explicit sm/md stay fixed; lg uses 14.5px text, 24px line height and 16px horizontal padding. See Input FieldSizes for every size and density. Opt-in `showCount` adds a visible aria-hidden counter and a localized accessible count description. `maxCount` is a soft limit that takes precedence over native `maxLength`; maxLength stays on the control and still blocks typing. Without either limit, only the count is shown. `countStrategy` replaces UTF-16 value.length, for example with UTF-8 byte counting. Over-limit text uses destructive-text and sets data-over-limit on the control without setting aria-invalid. Polite warnings announce only a new warning (80%) or over-limit zone after a 500ms typing pause, never on mount. The counter sits below the textarea, end-aligned; className stays on the textarea and cannot style the counter row. The clear button stays at the top end. See TextareaCounter for hard limits and a custom byte-counted soft limit.
author: gntik-ai
